newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan vice-president meets Egypt's Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Sudan vice-president meets Egypt's Mubarak.

text.p: Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Thursday, government officials said.
Their talks were expected to cover the military conflict in Sudan.

Sudan's Islamist military government has called for mobilisation against what it says are Ethiopian and rebel assaults on eastern Sudan. It has also accused neighbouring Eritrea of taking part in the fighting.
Saleh arrived in Cairo unexpectedly on Wednesday but the Egyptians have kept his schedule quiet.
Sudanese leader Hassan al-Turabi told Reuters on Wednesday that Saleh wanted to ask the Egyptian government about its decision to let opposition leaders use Cairo as their base.

The two major northern opposition leaders -- former prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi of the Umma Party and Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani of the Democratic Unionists -- have both been in Cairo for about two weeks.

Turabi, who is the speaker of parliament and the Islamist ideologue behind the military-dominated government, implied that Major-General Saleh would try to play on Egyptian concerns over the Nile waters, which pass through Sudan.
He said other Sudanese delegations would go to Saudi Arabia and other Middle Eastern countries but he did not give details.
Saleh is the most senior Sudanese to visit Egypt since President Omar Hassan al-Bashir came in June for an Arab summit.
Relations between the two countries have deteriorated recently, especially since Egypt said Sudan helped the Egyptian Islamists who tried to kill Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995. Sudan denies this.
